title: First bacteriophage genomes designed by a genome language model
summary: The Arc Institute group used Evo to design genomes resembling that of phage ΦX174: of 285 designs, 16 yielded functional phages (67–392 mutations from the closest natural one; 13 had never-seen mutations). They infect only two E. coli strains; a cocktail overcame resistance in three evolved strains. bioRxiv preprint; peer review is unconfirmed.

evidence.tested: Of 285 Evo-designed genomes, 16 were synthesized and gave functional phages in E. coli, and these were tested for fitness, host range and, for three resistant strains, a phage cocktail.
evidence.unknown: The source states host range was limited to E. coli C and W, all 16 phages were based on the phiX174 template, and clinical use is not shown.
evidence.ai_role: Evo, fine-tuned on Microviridae sequences, generated whole phage genomes resembling phiX174.
